status: Signed 2026-07-14; DEC must hold in abeyance incomplete discretionary permit applications for covered data centers until DPS submits the final Generic Environmental Impact Statement and findings statement.
key_provisions: Binding state-agency permitting restriction for data centers that consume or can consume 50 MW or more: DEC must hold incomplete discretionary permits, approvals, licenses, and similar permissions while DPS completes a statewide Generic Environmental Impact Statement; it does not override local permitting or zoning.
end_condition: Ends when DPS submits the final Generic Environmental Impact Statement and associated findings statement; the order excludes local-government permits, approvals, licenses, and similar permissions.

bill: Governor Abbott August 3, 2026 Data Center Audit Directive
status: Governor directive issued 2026-08-03; ERCOT implementation notice issued 2026-08-03.
key_provisions: Directs PUCT and ERCOT to verify and audit every data center advancing through ERCOT interconnection before it may move forward, pausing the Batch Zero process pending the required review.
end_condition: Until PUCT and ERCOT complete the comprehensive verification and audit; projects that fail applicable requirements must be denied grid connection.

sponsors: Sen. Phil King and Sen. Charles Schwertner; House sponsor Rep. Phil King
status: Passed Senate 2025-03-19 (with amendments); passed House 2025-05-27 (RV#3643); Senate concurred in House amendments 2025-05-29; signed by Governor 2025-06-20, effective immediately.
key_provisions: Requires PUCT/ERCOT large-load planning and interconnection standards; applies to large loads at a default 75 MW single-site threshold; addresses interconnection studies, cost allocation, co-location, and emergency curtailment
end_condition: Ongoing statutory large-load standards; no sunset in the enacted bill text.
